title: Turkish Lamb Kofte
subtitle: spiced lamb patties grilled or pan-fried
excerpt: Minced lamb mixed with onion, garlic, cumin, coriander, and cinnamon, shaped into long patties, and cooked in a hot pan or on a grill. Serve with yoghurt and flatbread. Quick, punchy, and easy.
sourceNotes: Kofte are eaten across Turkey, the Middle East, and Central Asia. The Turkish tradition of grilling spiced mince on skewers over charcoal is ancient and widespread across the region.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze shaped, uncooked kofte. Cook from frozen adding 5 extra minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch and freeze half shaped and uncooked.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the mixture the night before and refrigerate. Shape just before cooking.

content.text: Mix the meat with your hands until it is very well combined. The mixture needs to be sticky enough to hold its shape when squeezed. Chilling it before cooking makes it easier to handle.

items.prepNote: at least 20% fat for juicy kofte

content.text: Combine all the ingredients except the oil in a large bowl. Mix well with your hands for 2 minutes until very sticky and uniform.
Shape into 12 oval patties, about 10cm long and 3cm wide. Press firmly.
Heat oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat.
Cook the kofte for 3 to 4 minutes per side until well browned and cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes. Serve with yoghurt, tomatoes, and flatbread.

items.cause: Mixture not kneaded enough or too much onion
items.fix: Mix the meat more vigorously -- the protein strands need to develop to bind the mixture. Grate the onion finely to reduce moisture.
Use lamb mince with a higher fat content. Cook to just done -- the centre should be just cooked through, not grey all the way.
Lamb can handle bold seasoning. Fry a small piece of the raw mixture to test the flavour before shaping all the kofte.

content.text: Kofte are eaten across Turkey, the Balkans, the Middle East, South Asia, and Central Asia. The tradition of cooking spiced minced meat on a skewer or a flat grill goes back thousands of years across these regions. Turkish kofte vary by region -- some are mixed with breadcrumbs, others are entirely meat. The key is always the quality of the lamb and the balance of spice.
